Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace instructions and current evidence, then use the fish-control bookshelf and the wake-visual inspection skill before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll keep all changes inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t run CFD unless the workspace instructions explicitly make that part of validation.

The inherited guidance already shows a mature capture route, so this is a later iteration rather than a first architecture proposal. I’m now comparing the four sampled captures as mechanism variants—especially the strongest finite run against the weakest useful ablation—and checking both visual rows before deciding whether the bookshelf’s later-iteration consultation threshold is met.

The visual comparison shows all four policies are self-propelled and retain the same coherent alternating top-down wake and three-dimensional shed structures; there is no advection or instability. The decisive difference is control topology: the carrier-phase-residual policy reaches 5/2/1.2 L at 12.106/14.905/15.637 T and captures at 16.044 T, while the three terminal-only variants share 12.177/15.026/15.796 T and capture at 16.225 T. Its main unresolved cost is persistent carrier saturation (47.8% anterior acceleration residence and both joints reaching 260 deg/T), so I’m consulting the shelf for a bounded state-feedback mechanism aimed at actuator headroom without disturbing the observed route.

The shelf’s relevant invariant is phase separation, not a published gait: keep the fast joint-encoded carrier distinct from the slower target-route response before opening high-authority steering. I’m adopting only that one mechanism, because it is also the only sampled change that materially improved the trajectory; I’m not adding a new actuator guard without rollout evidence that it would preserve this carrier. I’ll record that transfer and the rejected terminal-only alternatives in the notes before touching the policy.

The candidate now uses the sampled winning carrier-phase residual and removes the prefilled short-window bearing lead. I also added a durable cross-candidate lesson that distinguishes route-changing phase separation from the two terminal-only no-ops. Next I’m validating the parameter contract and then invoking the workspace’s required check-runner; no CFD will be run.

The required check-runner configuration could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. I’m continuing with the exact three commands embedded in that configuration, run separately and without CFD, so the same validation contract is still exercised.

All three required checks pass when run directly: the notes/guidance semantic check, the Julia policy-contract smoke test, and the solver boundary check. The Julia command emitted only environment SSH-profile warnings and exited successfully. I’m doing the final scope/diff review now.

Produced one carrier-phase-residual target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

The candidate replaces the ineffective bearing-rate lead with joint-phase residualization, selected from the best sampled capture (`16.044T`, score `-0.058311`).

Validation passed:

- Guidance/notes semantic check
- Julia policy-contract smoke test
- Solver boundary check

The configured check-runner agent’s pinned model was unavailable, so I ran its exact three commands directly. No CFD was run.
